svg.aria-label: How to write ो: 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
svg.title: Writing ो
svg.desc: 3 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ो (devanagari), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Static.ttf. Stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer, class 55 (ो, o sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source note on variation: The recognizer stores native writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 42 of the 83 stored prototypes of the o sign (51%) are two pen-down strokes and 29 (35%) are three. 76 of the 83 (92%) draw the stem before the flag, and 58 of the 83 (70%) draw it downward and lift before the flag. 41 of those 58 start the flag at its upper-left tip and arc right and down, the way most writers draw the e sign (116 of 165), so the stem, a lift, and the flag from its upper-left tip is the commonest form, 41 of the 83 (49%). 40 of the 83 add a short top stroke, last in 33: the piece of headline the bundled font prints across the top of the stem (x 0 to 273). The path leaves that piece undrawn, so the strip shows it in grey: in a word it is part of the word's one headline, which native writers draw last, across the whole word (82% of the 2,706 consonant prototypes in the same recognizer). Each sign was written by itself, with no consonant beside it, so the traces fix the sign's own strokes but not when it is written against its consonant or the headline; the book draws the sign alone and composes no Devanagari word from it. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Devanagari outline of the sign on its own. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Handwriting varies by writer.
